commitResults.messageTitle: Level 4: Add Todo, Deadline, and Event types
commitResults.messageBody:
All tasks are a single Task with only a description and a done flag.

Users need three kinds of work: todos with no date, deadlines due by a
date/time, and events with a start and an end. Dates can stay as
strings at this increment.

Let's,
* add Todo, Deadline, and Event as subclasses of Task
* add tasks with todo, deadline /by, and event /from /to
* show [T], [D], and [E] (and by/from/to text) in list, mark, and unmark

Keeping dates as strings matches Level 4. Real date parsing can wait
until a later increment.

Bad input such as an empty todo or an unknown word either crashes the
chatbot or is treated as a new task.
Users need a clear error and a chance to try again, without the list
changing.
Handle invalid chatbot commands for the following cases:
* empty todo description
* unknown commands
* blank input
* deadline missing a name or /by
* event missing a name, /from, or /to
* mark/unmark with a missing, non-numeric, or out-of-range number
Catch WodanException in the main loop, print the message, and keep
listening. A chatbot-specific exception keeps these errors separate
from Java's built-in ones, and the messages say how to correct the
command.

Tasks can be added, listed, and marked, but there is no way to remove one.
Users need to delete a quest by its list number and see what was removed.
Add the following:
* a delete N command that removes that task from the list
* a confirmation that prints the removed task and the new list size
* toString() on Todo, Deadline, and Event so add, list, mark, unmark, and
  delete share one print format
* the same missing/invalid number checks used by mark and unmark
Each subclass owns its [T]/[D]/[E] line, so Wodan does not switch on type
when printing.

commitResults.messageTitle: A-Enums: Represent commands with Command enum
commitResults.messageBody:
The main loop switches on raw strings such as todo and delete.
A mistyped word is easy to miss, and every new command has to be added
as another quoted case.
Add the following:
* a Command enum for todo, deadline, event, list, mark, unmark, delete,
  and bye
* Command.parse to turn the first word into that enum
* a switch on Command instead of on String
An enum lists the legal commands in one place. Unknown words fail in
parse, and the compiler can catch a missing case.

commitResults.messageTitle: implement storage of deadline as LocalDateTime object.
Extract Ui to isolate console input and output from Wodan.
commitResults.messageBody:
Wodan still decides which replies to show, but all Scanner and System.out use now go through Ui. This is the first step of the Ui/Storage/Parser/TaskList split and keeps chatbot wording unchanged.

Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>

commitResults.messageTitle: Extract TaskList to encapsulate in-memory task operations.
commitResults.messageBody:
Wodan now adds, deletes, and queries tasks through TaskList instead of
mutating an ArrayList directly. Storage still reads and writes ArrayList
so file I/O stays separate from list operations.

Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>

commitResults.messageTitle: Extract Parser to interpret user command lines.
commitResults.messageBody:
Wodan now asks Parser for the command word, arguments, task objects, and
list numbers, so command-string rules live in one place instead of the
main loop. Reply text and list/storage updates stay in Wodan.

Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>

commitResults.messageTitle: Turn Wodan into a coordinator with constructor and run.
commitResults.messageBody:
Wodan now holds Ui, Storage, and TaskList, loads the save file in the
constructor, and runs the command loop from run(). Storage takes the
file path from Wodan so the save location is no longer hardcoded there.

Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>

commitResults.messageTitle: Replace the command switch with Command objects.
commitResults.messageBody:
Wodan now parses a line into a Command and calls execute/isExit, so each
user action lives in its own class. The old Command enum is renamed to
CommandWord so Parser can still map the first token. Printed output is
unchanged; run() does not wrap every reply in extra divider lines.

Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>

commitResults.messageTitle: Add find task by keyword feature.

commitResults.messageBody:
The app assumes constructors and methods receive valid fields and arguments.

Adding assert statements helps to point at the broken assumptions and identity errors in the code.

Let's
* assert non-null task descriptions, event start/end order, and midnight storage for date-only values
* assert joinWithOr receives at least one word
* assert mark.unmark numbers exist in the list, and that status icons match after markAsDone/markAsUndone

Use Java assert for programmer mistakes. Keep user-facing checks as WodanExceptions so they still run when assertions are disabled.

Enable assertions with -ea when running the app.

commitResults.messageTitle: Task: Share mark and status methods
commitResults.messageBody:
Todo, Deadline, and Event each copy the same mark, unmark, status icon,
and description methods.

Copied methods drift apart when one subclass is updated and the others
are not. All three types share this behavior; only display and storage
encoding differ.

Let's move markAsDone, markAsUndone, getStatusIcon, and getDescription
into Task as concrete methods and delete the copies.

Inheritance is the simplest way to share this behavior because every
task already extends Task.

Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>

Task description and isDone, and the date fields on Deadline and Event,
are protected even though subclasses only need to read them.

Protected fields let any subclass write those values directly, which
widens the chance of inconsistent state. Code quality guidelines ask
to define variables in the least possible scope.

Let's make those fields private and read them through getters.

A getter keeps the same information available without exposing
writable fields to subclasses.

Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>

occursOn combines two negated date comparisons in one expression.

Double negatives such as !isBefore and !isAfter are easy to misread,
so the inclusive range is harder to verify. The guideline is to
evaluate complicated expressions in named steps.

Let's store the start-bound and end-bound checks in local booleans
before combining them.

The comparisons stay the same, including dates on the start and end
days.

Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>

commitResults.messageTitle: Task: Name the status icon characters
commitResults.messageBody:
getStatusIcon returns "X" or a space as raw literals.

Those characters are magic strings: a reader has to infer that "X"
means done and a space means not done. Named constants make the
meaning obvious.

Let's introduce STATUS_DONE_ICON and STATUS_NOT_DONE_ICON and return
them from getStatusIcon.

Display text stays [X] and [ ] as before.

Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>

commitResults.messageTitle: Task: Name save-file type and done flags
commitResults.messageBody:
Save-file lines use T, D, E and 0/1 as raw literals in three task
classes and in Storage.

Those letters are magic strings, so a typo in one class can write a
line the loader will skip. Named constants keep encoding and decoding
on the same tokens.

Let's add STORAGE_TYPE_* and STORAGE_DONE/STORAGE_NOT_DONE, and build
the shared prefix in Task.toStoragePrefix.

The on-disk format is unchanged.

Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>

commitResults.messageTitle: Parser: Split a command line once
commitResults.messageBody:
parseCommandWord and parseArguments each trim and split the same
input line.

The two splits can disagree if one path is edited later, and a
reader has to check both methods to see how a line is tokenized.
The guideline is to avoid duplication and not trip the reader.

Let's trim and split in one helper, then parse the command word and
arguments from that array.

Empty-line errors stay a WodanException with the same message.

Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>

Deadline and event parsing repeats /by, /from, and /to in regexes,
startsWith checks, and error text.

Those markers are magic strings. A mismatch between the split pattern
and the error example would confuse users and hide a parser bug.

Let's define BY_MARKER, FROM_MARKER, TO_MARKER and the matching split
patterns, and build messages from those constants.

The wording shown to the user is unchanged.

Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>

parseEvent mixes splitting, validation, and Event construction in one
long method, including a nested from/to special case.

A reader cannot see the happy path at a glance, and the method is well
past the point where shortening is recommended. SLAP asks each fragment
to stay at one level of abstraction.

Let's validate the description, split the times, then validate the
times in helpers, and keep parseEvent as that sequence.

Error messages stay the same, including the shared EVENT_USAGE hint.

Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>

commitResults.messageTitle: Storage: Split save-file parsing by type
commitResults.messageBody:
parseTask checks field counts, dates, and type codes in one switch,
so the method is long and mixes several levels of detail.

A reader has to hold todo, deadline, and event rules at once. The
guideline is to shorten methods past about 30 lines and keep one
level of abstraction in a fragment.

Let's dispatch on type, then parse each kind in its own helper, with
named field-count constants.

Corrupt lines are still skipped; the save format is unchanged.

Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>

The console welcome and the GUI greeting each hard-code the same two
sentences.

Similar text that lives in two places can drift, so CLI and GUI would
greet the user differently. The guideline is not to trip the reader
with similar things that look different.

Let's keep the hail and prompt as Ui constants and build both UIs
from those strings.

Wording and indent are unchanged.

Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>

tryParse nests two try-catch blocks when the text contains T.

The extra nesting hides the fallback from ISO local date-time to the
save-file formatter. The guideline is to avoid deep nesting and keep
the happy path easy to follow.

Let's parse each ISO form in sequence in a helper, with a comment in
the first catch to explain the fallback.

Invalid text still returns null, same as before.

Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>

stripLeadingIndent uses {4,8} in a regex with no explanation.

Those numbers are magic: they encode how many leading spaces Ui
prints, so a later indent change would silently break GUI replies.
Named constants make the coupling visible.

Let's introduce MIN_CONSOLE_INDENT and MAX_CONSOLE_INDENT and build
the regex from them.

Replies in the GUI still lose the same 4 to 8 leading spaces.

Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>

commitResults.messageTitle: Parser: Trim a task number once
commitResults.messageBody:
parseTaskNumber calls arguments.trim() three times for the same text.

Repeating the trim makes it look as if each check might see a
different string. The guideline is to structure related steps so the
story is obvious.

Let's trim into one local variable and reuse it for the empty check,
parse, and error text.

Validation and messages stay the same.

Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>

Public STORAGE_* and GREETING_* constants sit after private static
fields in Task and Ui.

Checkstyle DeclarationOrder, and the coding standard, expect public
members before private ones so the class header is consistent.

Let's declare the public constants first, then the private static
fields.

Behavior is unchanged.

Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>

commitResults.messageTitle: Use Java streams for list processing Find, on, save, and load walk lists with for-loops that filter or transform elements. A-Streams asks to use Java Streams where that is a natural fit. filter, map, and collect express those steps without a mutable accumulator. Let's, * collect matching 1-based task numbers with IntStream filter/map * load and save tasks with stream filter/map/collect * trim save-file fields and join command names with streams Leave command printing as for-loops because those loops exist to call the UI, not to build a collection. Chatbot output is unchanged.
